children: Shares of Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Ltd., the passenger vehicle arm of Tata Motors, will be in focus on Tuesday, September 1, after brokerage firm Kotak Institutional Equities retained its 'Sell' recommendation on the stock.
Kotak has set a price target of ₹285 per share, implying a downside of nearly 10% from Tata Motors PV's previous closing price of ₹316.50 per share.

The brokerage remains negative on Tata Motors PV, citing intensifying competitive pressures at Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) as electrification gains momentum across the European Union and the UK, while Chinese automakers expand their presence in the premium segment.
Kotak also flagged execution risks from JLR's strategic pivot towards the US, particularly given the absence of local manufacturing.

The brokerage highlighted balance sheet pressures associated with the electric vehicle transition and expects a gradual recovery in margins as headwinds from foreign exchange, variable marketing expenses (VME), warranty costs and depreciation persist. It added that benefits from a favourable product mix have largely peaked.
On the domestic front, Kotak expects Tata Motors PV's market share to be close to its peak, while profitability remains the weakest among peers.
Of the 32 analysts that have coverage on Tata Motors PV, 13 of them have a 'Buy' rating, 10 have a 'Hold' rating, while nine have a 'Sell' call on the stock.
Shares of Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles settled 0.78% lower at ₹316.50 on Monday.

title: Five factors why Kotak remains bearish on this Tata Motors unit
